questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another car), use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see, and wear reflective materials to be visible. Change your lane position based on conditions to see better, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from everything except:
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also protects you if you crash.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles ride in a staggered formation, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Riders on three-wheel motorcycles should travel one behind the other in a single-file line.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to their other safety benefits.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the brake smoothly.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake right away and re-apply it smoothly.

questions.question: Texas law requires motorcycles to have certain equipment. Which item is NOT required?
questions.explanation: Texas law requires motorcycles to have a horn, mirror, steering mechanism, brakes, tires, wheels, exhaust system, tail lamp, stop lamp, license plate lamp, rear red reflector, and headlamp. The motorcycle must also have proper identification numbers.

questions.question: When riding in a lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your fingers on the clutch lever and brakes. This reduces the time needed to react to hazards.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel for maximum braking power in a straight line.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane when riding in traffic. Swerving into other lanes to avoid a small animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. It is safer to hit a small animal than to cause a crash with another driver.

questions.question: What should a rider do when entering a turn?

options.text: Lean their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a turn. Release the throttle and use both brakes if needed.

questions.question: In Texas, who is required to wear a helmet?

options.text: All motorcycle and moped operators and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: All motorcycle and moped operators and passengers.
questions.explanation: In Texas, all motorcycle and moped operators and passengers must wear helmets. Some exemptions may apply.

questions.question: Should motorcycle riders wear hearing protection?

options.text: Yes, always wear it to prevent hearing damage.
Only wear it on long rides.
No, it blocks horns and sirens.
No, a helmet provides enough protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always wear it to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing loss, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still allowing you to hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve the bike away from hazards.

questions.explanation: Release the brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if you lock the rear brake on a good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: On a good road surface, you can keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to accelerate out of a wobble.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists enters a highway or curve, how should they ride?

options.text: In the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.
